newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Ariane to carry satellites for Arabs, Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Ariane to carry satellites for Arabs, Malaysia.

text.p: Western Europe's 92nd Ariane rocket is scheduled to blast off from French Guiana on Wednesday carrying telecommunications satellites for the Arab League and Malaysia, officials of the Arianespace company said on Monday.
ARABSAT 2B weighs 2.6 tonnes and was built by a consortium led by France's Aerospatiale for the 21-nation Arab League.
MEASAT 2 is the second in a series of satellites for Malaysia's Binariang Group. It weighs 1.5 tonnes and was built by Los Angeles-based Hughes Space & Communications.
The satellites will be launched aboard an Ariane 44L rocket equipped with four liquid strap-on boosters -- the most powerful in the Ariane-4 series.
The launch is set for between 2240 and 2326 GMT.

It will be the fifth Ariane mission since last June's explosion of the first new generation Ariane-5 rocket, 37 seconds after its maiden launch from the European Space Agency (ESA) launch centre in Kourou, French Guiana on the northeast coast of South America.
